alerts.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 26 at 4:10PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
alerts.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Wednesday August 26 to 400 PM Thursday August 27

IMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front
Range Urban Corridor.  Ozone concentrations in the Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups category are possible both Wednesday and Thursday
during the afternoon and evening hours. The best chance for these
elevated ozone levels will be in western parts of the Denver metro
area, including the adjacent foothills.  For Colorado air quality
conditions, forecasts, and advisories, visit:
https://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx   If
possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until at least 4 p.m.
Thursday, August 27, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone
pollution through state policies. For more information about
health impacts and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone-pollution-and-your-health

HEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms
and breathing discomfort in active children and adults and people
with lung disease, such as asthma. Active children and adults, and
people with lung disease, such as asthma, should reduce prolonged
or heavy outdoor exertion during the afternoons and evenings both
Wednesday and Thursday.

alerts.headline: Flood Advisory issued August 26 at 4:03PM MDT until August 26 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Larimer County in north central Colorado...
including the Cameron Peak Burn Scar.

* WHEN...Until 700 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 403 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has
fallen.

- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Buckhorn Creek, North Fork Fish Creek, Cedar Creek, Sheep Creek,
Eld Creek and Miller Fork. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.50
inches are expected over the area. This additional rain will
result in minor flooding.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Southeastern Larimer County including the
Cameron Peak Burn Scar.

alerts.headline: Flood Advisory issued August 26 at 3:06PM MDT until August 26 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Debris flows and flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Central Larimer County in north central Colorado, including
parts of the Cameron Peak burn area.

* WHEN...Until 600 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Debris flows causing minor flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 304 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Central Larimer County.

afd.snippet: 000 FXUS65 KBOU 261740 AFDBOU Area Forecast Discussion National Weather Service Denver/Boulder CO 1140 AM MDT Wed Aug 26 2026 .KEY MESSAGES... - Scattered afternoon/evening thunderstorms expected for theI-25 Corridor and plains. A few storms could become severe, with large hail and strong winds possible. - Thunderstorm coverage decreases Thursday and Friday with mainly isolated high-based showers/

fwf.snippet: .DISCUSSION...Rest of today through Thursday...Scattered thunderstorms will move across the urban corridor and eastern plains late this afternoon and early evening with heavy rain, hail, and strong winds. Warmer and drier air moves in for Thursday with isolated high-based showers/thunderstorms. Gusty outflow winds will accompany the showers/thunderstorms while any rainfall will be light. LONG TERM
